Cleans tracking parameters from links and checks link safety, entirely on this device.

What it does
Strips tracking parameters from links before you share or open them, follows shortened links and AMP pages to their real destination, and can check whether a link looks safe — all without ever opening it.

Supported platforms
Facebook, Messenger, YouTube, Instagram, Twitter/X, TikTok, LinkedIn, Snapchat, Reddit, Pinterest, Amazon, Google, Spotify, and Threads each have their own tracking parameters recognized and removed. Generic trackers (utm_* campaign tags, ad-click IDs, email-marketing IDs, cross-site analytics IDs) are stripped from any site, not just the ones listed.

Shortened and AMP links
Known link-shortener domains, Facebook /share/ links, and Google AMP pages are resolved to their real destination automatically, so you see exactly where a link actually goes.

Safety checks (optional, each toggled independently in Settings)
• Google Safe Browsing and VirusTotal — bring your own free API key
• Domain age check — free, no key needed, flags domains registered very recently
• URL-shape and permission-request scanning — built in, works with no key at all, catches things like lookalike domains, raw IP addresses, and pages that immediately ask for camera/microphone/location access

Instant share-and-clean
Pick Tracker Remover from any app's Share menu and it cleans the link and reopens the Share sheet right away, with no need to open the app itself.

History
Every cleaned link, what was removed from it, and its safety verdict is saved locally so you can look back at it later. Turn this off or clear it anytime in Settings.

Privacy
This app has no backend server. Everything happens on your own device. History and any API keys you add are stored in local app storage only, and are deleted the moment you uninstall the app. See Privacy Policy for full details.

What this app does and doesn\'t collect
How your data is (and isn\'t) handled

Tracker Remover does not collect, transmit, or sell any usage data, analytics, or personal information. There is no analytics SDK, crash reporter, or advertising SDK in this app.

What stays on your device:
• Cleaned-link history (the original link, cleaned link, domain, and timestamp) is stored only in a local database on your phone. Turn it off or clear it anytime in Settings.
• Safe Browsing and VirusTotal API keys, if you add them, are stored only in local app storage on your device.

What leaves your device (only if you turn it on):
• If you enable Safe Browsing, VirusTotal, or the domain-age check in Settings, the link you're cleaning (not your history, not your keys) is sent directly from your device to that service's own servers (Google, VirusTotal, or the RDAP registry) to get a verdict. Those requests go straight to them, not through any server run by this app's developer, because there is no such server.
• Following a shortened link (bit.ly, t.co, etc.) to find its real destination also requires a direct connection from your device to that link's host.

That's the complete list. Nothing else is sent anywhere.

Last updated: 2026

Tracker Remover is a personal, self-contained app. This policy describes exactly what happens to your data, because there isn't much to describe.

1. No developer-run server
This app has no backend server. Nothing you do in this app is sent to, logged by, or stored by its developer, because there is nowhere for it to go.

2. What's stored locally on your device
• Cleaned-link history: original link, cleaned link, domain, timestamp, and safety verdict, stored in a local database on your phone only.
• Settings and API keys you enter: stored in local app storage on your device only.
You can clear history or turn off saving it at any time in Settings. Uninstalling the app deletes all of it.

3. What's sent over the network, and to whom
These only happen for the specific action you take, and go directly from your device to the third party, never through the developer:
• Resolving a shortened link: a request to that link's own host to follow its redirect.
• Google Safe Browsing (only if you enable it and add a key): the link is sent to Google's Safe Browsing API.
• VirusTotal (only if you enable it and add a key): the link is sent to VirusTotal's API.
• Domain age check (only if enabled): the domain is sent to a public RDAP lookup service.
Each of the above is governed by that third party's own privacy policy, not this one.

4. Your API keys
If you add your own Safe Browsing or VirusTotal API key, it's used only to make the request described above and is never sent anywhere else.

5. Children's privacy
This app doesn't knowingly collect data from anyone, so this doesn't change for children.

6. Changes to this policy
If this policy changes, the updated version will ship with a new app version.

7. Contact
Questions about this policy can be sent through the Feedback option in Settings.

Last updated: 2026

By using Tracker Remover, you agree to the following:

1. What this app does
Tracker Remover strips known tracking parameters from links, can follow shortened links to their real destination, and can optionally check a link's safety using services you enable and provide your own API keys for.

2. No warranty
This app is provided "as is," without warranty of any kind. Safety checks (Safe Browsing, VirusTotal, domain age) are best-effort signals, not guarantees — a link marked safe can still turn out to be harmful, and the absence of a check result never means a link is unsafe. Use your own judgment before opening or sharing any link.

3. Your responsibility
You're responsible for any API keys you add and for complying with the terms of the services those keys belong to (Google Safe Browsing, VirusTotal). You're responsible for how you use cleaned or shared links.

4. No liability
The developer isn't liable for any damage or loss resulting from use of this app, to the fullest extent permitted by law.

5. Open source
This app's source code is available under the terms in its repository (see Source Code in Settings).

6. Changes
These terms may change in future versions of the app. Continued use after an update means you accept the current terms.

7. Contact
Questions can be sent through the Feedback option in Settings.
